newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil setting up credit risk centre.
newsitem.headline: Brazil setting up credit risk centre.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) Thursday approved the setting up of a consumer and corporate credit risk centre, to be run by the Central Bank, officials said.
Alkimar Moura, Central Bank Director of Controls, said the CMN decision was the first step towards establishing a full-blown register of indebtedness for banks to refer to.
"The aim of this centre is to provide information on the debt of companies and individuals," Moura said.
From June 30, banks will be obliged to inform the Central Bank of all loans above 50,000 reais to either individuals or companies, naming the recipients.
For loans under 50,000 reais, the banks will have to provide at the end of each month the value of total credits but will not have to give information on the recipient.
Moura said that eventually, banks would be able to consult the register so long as their clients gave them permission to do so.
From next year, the CMN hopes that banks will be able to identify the group that individual companies belong to so the Central Bank can paint a complete picture of corporate indebtedness.
Brazil's banks have notoriously high bad-debt ratios because of poor lending controls and the Central Bank has been studying ways to reduce credit risk and shore up the banking system.
